name: Genetic Malformation Syndrome with Odontal and/or Periodontal Component
aliases: Syndrome with Dental and Periodontal Anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Genetic Malformation Syndrome with Odontal and/or Periodontal Component

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic dental anomalies including enamel hypoplasia, malformed crowns, and delayed eruption
Early-onset periodontitis with alveolar bone loss disproportionate to plaque levels
Identification of pathogenic variant in associated gene(s) by molecular genetic testing
Presence of craniofacial anomalies such as midface hypoplasia or cleft palate
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two major criteria including odontal malformations and early-onset periodontitis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical criteria are met

pathognomonic.symptomName: Enamel hypoplasia with pitted and grooved dental surfaces
Severe early-onset periodontitis with alveolar bone resorption
Delayed eruption of primary and permanent teeth

common.symptomName: Malformed tooth crowns including microdontia and taurodontism
searchTerms: teeth with unusual size or shape

common.symptomName: Midface hypoplasia with flattened nasal bridge
searchTerms: low nasal bridge with small midface

common.symptomName: Gingival inflammation disproportionate to plaque accumulation

searchTerms: split or hole in roof of mouth

occasional.symptomName: Root malformations including shortened or tapered roots
Mild hearing loss due to craniofacial anomalies
searchTerms: mild hearing loss from face shape
slight deafness due to craniofacial issues
hearing difficulties linked to facial anomalies

occasional.symptomName: Mild speech difficulties related to palatal anomalies
searchTerms: speech difficulties due to mouth shape
slight talking issues related to palate

rare.symptomName: Congenital heart defects such as septal defects
searchTerms: holes in heart present at birth

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers in gingival crevicular fluid
imaging: Panoramic dental X-rays showing root malformations and alveolar bone loss
CT scan revealing craniofacial structural anomalies
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes involved in tooth development and periodontal tissue integrity (e.g., DLX3, MSX1)
other: Histopathology of gingival tissue showing chronic inflammatory infiltrate with connective tissue destruction

distinguishingFeatures: Primarily enamel defects without significant periodontal involvement

redFlags: Rapid alveolar bone loss leading to premature tooth loss
Presence of craniofacial malformations with dental anomalies
Family history of similar dental and periodontal abnormalities
references: Orphanet: Genetic Malformation Syndrome with Odontal and/or Periodontal Component, ORPHA:183580
Witkop CJ Jr. Hereditary defects of enamel. J Oral Pathol. 1988;17(1):1-9.
Hart TC, Hart PS. Genetic basis of periodontal disease. Periodontol 2000. 2007;43:79-94.
